questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: Why we wear uniforms and how they can change our behaviour
The history of the police force in London and New York
How to choose the right clothes for a job interview
Why school uniforms should be banned in all schools
questions.why: Neil and Tim discuss the point of uniforms and how wearing one can let you behave differently.

questions.q: Why is Tim wearing a police officer's hat?
options: He has a new job with the police
He found it in the studio
It protects him from the sun
To get in the mood for the topic
questions.why: Tim says he's wearing it 'to get me in the mood for our topic today – uniforms!'

questions.q: Why do the police and emergency services wear uniforms?
options: Because they are cheaper than normal clothes for work
They need practical clothes and must be easy to recognise
To look more fashionable and modern on television
To keep them warm and dry when working at night
questions.why: Neil says they need practical clothes, and Tim adds that people need to recognise them.

questions.q: What else can a uniform do, according to Neil?
options: Make you work longer hours
Help you earn more money
Show that you belong to a group
Stop you making friends at work
questions.why: Neil says a uniform lets you fit in and shows you belong to a group or organisation.

questions.q: What does cultural historian Joe Moran say about wearing a uniform?
options: It makes people feel less important than others
It is uncomfortable for most people to wear all day
It shows your true personality to the people around you
It is like putting on a mask, which can feel freeing
questions.why: He compares it to the freedom of masks and says taking on a professional role 'can be liberating'.

questions.q: What example does Neil give of how a uniform might help someone?
options: A shy person might behave more confidently
A lazy person might work harder
A tall person might look shorter
A new worker might learn faster
questions.why: Neil says if you're shy, a uniform might feel liberating because you can act more confidently.

questions.q: Which uniform and persona would Tim choose?
options: A surgeon
A police officer
An airline pilot
A chef
questions.why: Tim says he'd choose an airline pilot, with a blazer, cap and mirror sunglasses.

questions.q: What uniform would Neil like to try?
options: A nun's habit
A chef's uniform
A pilot's blazer
A surgeon's scrubs
questions.why: Neil says he'd go for a chef's apron, checked trousers and a tall hat.
